about: W1, Gate duty (for-review/design/faction-quests.md, 2.2). One shift on the foot lane in the Gate Yard for Sergeant Rook: five come up the tunnel before the bell, and the fourth is Calla Wynn, a medic with a forged tag. Marks: w1 (1 offered and heard, 2 on the lane, 100 done), w1.q (who is at the head of the lane: 1 to 5, 6 when the last is through), w1.toll (litres in the tin), w1.short (people through with no litre taken), wynn (1 held by the book, 2 bought a real tag, 3 waved through, 4 her water taken and then held), wynn.took (her 12 L taken). Rook is at the Gate Yard here and not off shift at the Last Call, which is not built. Rook and Calla Wynn have bodies of their own since 25 November (TOWN in Tools/build_gut_metahuman.py).
name: Gate duty
giver: Sergeant Rook, at the tally desk in the Gate Yard
steps: Sergeant Rook wants a reader on the foot lane until the bell. Tell him you will stand it, at the tally desk in the Gate Yard.
Stand at the head of the foot lane, east of the barrier in the Gate Yard. Read each tag as they come up the tunnel and take a litre a head. When the last is through, take the count to Rook.
You stood the shift. The bell was rung for the gate, and Rook paid you.

Sergeant Rook.words: You are off Rask's ladder. I know the brand. I am a reader short on the foot lane, and there is an hour of people still to come up that tunnel before the bell. One shift. Twenty-five litres, and a share of the tin.

answers.words: What is the work?
I will stand it.
Not tonight.

Sergeant Rook.words: Everybody who comes up shows a tag. You read it. A litre a head goes in the tin. No tag is property: you stand them by the post, and I send them up the stair. Nobody goes through on a story. That is all of it, and you would be surprised how few can fucking do it.
Foot lane. East side of the barrier, at its head. They come up one at a time. Read the tag, take the litre, send them on. Bring me the count when the last of them is through.
Sergeant Rook.log: Took a shift reading tags on the foot lane for Sergeant Rook of the Wardens.

Sergeant Rook.words: The lane is that way. The count comes to me when the last of them is through, and not before.
That is the last of them. Count.

answers.words: Five came up, and the tin is right.
Five came up. The tin is short.

Sergeant Rook.words: Then it is right. A fifth of the tin is the reader's.
Short comes out of the reader. That is the lane's rule, and it was the rule before I had the lane. No share.

And the medic with the doubled stamp. By the book. She goes up on tomorrow's bill, and the post's share of her is yours: eight litres. Twenty-five for the shift. And one fine at the post's discretion, the next time you earn one.
Sergeant Rook.log: Stood the shift at the gate. Rook paid 25 L, and 8 L more for Calla Wynn.

Sergeant Rook.words: You bought a stranger a tag out of your own water. The book has no line for that, and no rule against it. She is on the register. Twenty-five for the shift, and one fine at the post's discretion, the next time you earn one.
Sergeant Rook.log: Stood the shift at the gate. Rook paid 25 L.

Sergeant Rook.words: Five tags read. Give me a moment with the book.

I count heads as well as litres. Five came up, and four of them have a number in the register. I will not ask you which. Twenty-five for the shift, because you stood it. Do not ever fucking do that on my lane again.
Sergeant Rook.log: Stood the shift at the gate. Rook paid 25 L, and knows somebody went through unread.

Sergeant Rook.words: Five and five. Twenty-five for the shift, and one fine at the post's discretion, the next time you earn one.
Sergeant Rook.log: Stood the shift at the gate. Rook paid 25 L.

Sergeant Rook.words: The Row's cut is due at the end of the week, and I will want somebody the bars do not know. Not tonight. The gate is down.

lines.words: Guild hauler. Ridgeline to the Flats and back, since before you had that brand. Tag is on the cord. Litre is in my hand.
lines.note: The tag is the Pump's strike: one clean blow, and a number.

answers.words: One litre. Through.
What is out on the Flats tonight?

lines.words: Wind. A convoy stuck on the salt with its lights off, and people out there who are waiting for the lights to go on. Same shit as every night.
New reader. Do not let them rush you. The ones who rush you are the ones to read twice.
Tag is good. It is good, look at it. I have not got the litre. I had it this morning. I can bring it down tomorrow, first thing, I swear on the pipe.
lines.note: The tag is good. She has nothing in her hands.

answers.words: Then you wait outside until somebody pays it for you.
I will put your litre in the tin. (1 L)
Go through. Bring it tomorrow.

lines.words: Out there? At night? You know what the fuck is out there at night.
You... all right. I will not forget who did that.
Tomorrow. First thing. Thank you.
Chainmen. I do not pay at the lane. The Block settles with the post by the month. Ask your sergeant, when you have been here longer than a fucking hour.
lines.note: The tag is good. On his belt hang four empty collars.

answers.words: The post takes a litre from everybody. Pay.
Go through.

lines.words: A litre. I will remember a litre. Harrow remembers them for me.
Quick learner.
Calla Wynn. Medic. Twelve litres on me, and I can set a bone. The tag is good. It is good.
lines.note: The stamp on her tag is doubled: struck twice, and the second blow slipped. It is a forgery, and a poor one.

answers.words: This was struck twice. Who sold it to you?
No tag means property. Stand by the post.
answers.log: Held Calla Wynn, a medic, at the gate for a forged tag. No tag means property.

answers.words: The post strikes tags for the Pump. I will buy you a real one. (30 L)
answers.log: Bought Calla Wynn a real tag at the gate, for 30 L of my own.

answers.words: Go through. I never read it.
answers.log: Waved Calla Wynn through the gate on a forged tag.

answers.words: Twelve litres, you said. Give it here, and I did not see the stamp.
answers.log: Took 12 L off Calla Wynn at the gate to look away from a forged tag.

lines.words: A man at the Drive-In. Everything I had but the twelve. He said it was off the Pump's own die. I have walked four days on that. Please.
All of it? That is... here. That is everything. Now let me by.

answers.words: Go through.
No tag means property. Stand by the post.

lines.words: I set bones. I would have set yours.
Thirty litres. For somebody you have known for a minute. Wynn. Remember it. I will remember yours.
Thank you. I will not forget the lane, or who was reading on it.
You are worse than the bastard at the Drive-In. He at least sold me something.
You took it and... of course. Of course you fucking did.
Pump cart, east branch. Tag, litre. I am the last: there is nobody behind me but the dark.

answers.words: One litre. Through.
East branch. How is the water?

lines.words: You did not hear it from a cart hand. The east tank is down a hand's width since Tuesday, and nobody has drawn from it. Work that out.
Ring your bell, reader. That is the day.
You. Sit down. No, sit. Somebody who fights for Rask does not get to say he is fine. I have slats and binding, and you have thirty litres of credit with me that I intend to work off.
lines.log: Calla Wynn, tagged and working on Main Street, gave me a splint.

lines.words: The stall lets me work by her fire. When you are hurt, come to me before you go to the cutter. He charges for the saw.

people.name: Calla Wynn
people.prompt: Talk to the woman by the fire

lines.words: I do not know you. I never came up any lane. But there are people under the dam who know who was reading that night, and they have long memories for a kindness.
Twelve litres. I am counting the days it takes to earn it back, and your face is at the top of every one of them.

people.name: Calla Wynn
people.prompt: Talk to the woman held by the water cart

lines.words: Lot nine, tomorrow. Medic, it says on the card. Eighteen litres and six for the skill. I set bones. You read a stamp, and now I am twenty-four litres of somebody else's.
They did not find the twelve litres on me. I told the clerk a reader had it. She wrote that down. She writes everything down.

tally.words: Told Rook you will stand the shift
Tags read at the head of the foot lane
